newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: S'pore oil products see jet fuel down, gas oil up.
newsitem.headline: S'pore oil products see jet fuel down, gas oil up.

text.p: Singapore oil products were mixed on Friday, with jet fuel under further pressure, while gas oil, fuel oil and light distillates were firmer, traders said.

A US trader who offered jet fuel on Friday, continued to offer as low as $28.20 for 100,000 barrels lifting September 14-18. The cargo was eventually sold to a European major at $28. The major resold the cargo to a Singapore trader at 50 cents higher. Traders said the anticipated correction in jet prices, which has long been described as "overpriced", was due to supplies previously in storage offered in Asia. But they said a freefall in jet prices would be curbed by strong gas oil prices.

Traders said the rally in 0.5 percent sulphur gas oil prices were due to tight MidEast supplies on a combination of reasons. They said domestic MidEast demand has risen despite increased refining capacities especially in Kuwait. Jordan has also recently shifted its purchases to Saudi Arabia following recent riots while Iran has been rumored to have bought gas oil from a western major in Saudi Arabia. Tight Mediterranean supplies and high prices also prompted traders to shift their purchases to the MidEast to supply to East Africa. Singapore physical gas oil jumped 35 cents from Thursday with an offer at $26 for end-September facing bids ranging between $25.75 and $26.

Gasoline traders raised their bids with the hikes in crude although the sentiment remained bearish as regional demand is limited to Taiwan whose tender for second-half September reformate closes on September 3. A western trader raised his bid through the day from $21.60 a barrel for 50,000 barrels of 95-octane unleaded lifting second-half September to trade at $22.50 at the day's end. Similarly, the bid for a 92-octane unleaded cargo was raised from $20.70 to $21.00, much firmer from Thursday's deal level at $20.50. Fuel oil rose 50 cents a tonne on firmer crudes and limited MidEast supplies. The 180-380 cst spread narrowed to $4. -- RAMTHAN HUSSAIN (+65-8703086)
